name: Question 12
problem:
The vector-valued function $f(\theta ,ϕ),$ given by 

$$
f(\theta ,ϕ)=⟨4\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,\text{_____},\,4\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ⟩
$$

parametrizes the hyperboloid of one sheet defined in Cartesian coordinates as ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}=16.$ By expressing the equation of the hyperboloid in cylindrical polar coordinates, determine the second component of $f.$

*Hint: You may use the fact that the hyperbola ${r}^{2}-{z}^{2}={k}^{2}$ can be parametrized as $⟨r,z⟩=⟨k\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ,k\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ⟩$* for $ϕ\in R.$
worked_solution:
If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical coordinates of a point and $(x,y,z)$ are the corresponding Cartesian coordinates of that point, then we have

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

Substituting this into our equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-{z}^{2} & =16 \\ (r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}-{z}^{2} & =16 \\ {r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )-{z}^{2} & =16 \\ {r}^{2}-{z}^{2} & =16.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, the hyperbola ${r}^{2}-{z}^{2}=16$ represents the intersection of our hyperboloid with the plane that passes through the $z$-axis and makes the angle of $\theta $ with the positive $x$-axis. Using the hint, a parametrization of such hyperbola can be given as

$$
⟨r,z⟩=⟨4\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ,\,4\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ⟩,\,ϕ\in R.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\theta ,ϕ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z⟩ \\  & =⟨(4\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,(4\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,4\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨4\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,4\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,4\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $\theta \in [0,2\pi )$ and $ϕ\in R.$

Therefore, the second component of $f$ is $4\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .$

The vector-valued function f(θ,ϕ), given by

f(θ,ϕ)=⟨4cosh⁡ϕcos⁡θ,_____,4sinh⁡ϕ⟩

parametrizes the hyperboloid of one sheet defined in Cartesian coordinates as x2+y2−z2=16. By expressing the equation of the hyperboloid in cylindrical polar coordinates, determine the second component of f.

Hint: You may use the fact that the hyperbola r2−z2=k2 can be parametrized as ⟨r,z⟩=⟨kcosh⁡ϕ,ksinh⁡ϕ⟩ for ϕ∈R.

a
cosh⁡ϕsin⁡θ
b
4sinh⁡ϕcos⁡θ
c
4sinh⁡ϕsin⁡θ
d
sinh⁡ϕcos⁡θ
e
4cosh⁡ϕsin⁡θ

EXPLANATION

If (r,θ,z) are the cylindrical coordinates of a point and (x,y,z) are the corresponding Cartesian coordinates of that point, then we have

x=rcos⁡θ,y=rsin⁡θ,z=z.

Substituting this into our equation, we get

x2+y2−z2=16(rcos⁡θ)2+(rsin⁡θ)2−z2=16r2(cos2⁡θ+sin2⁡θ)−z2=16r2−z2=16.

Here, the hyperbola r2−z2=16 represents the intersection of our hyperboloid with the plane that passes through the z-axis and makes the angle of θ with the positive x-axis. Using the hint, a parametrization of such hyperbola can be given as

⟨r,z⟩=⟨4cosh⁡ϕ,4sinh⁡ϕ⟩,ϕ∈R.

Now, for any point (x,y,z) on our surface, we obtain the following:

f(θ,ϕ)=⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨rcos⁡θ,rsin⁡θ,z⟩=⟨(4cosh⁡ϕ)cos⁡θ,(4cosh⁡ϕ)sin⁡θ,4sinh⁡ϕ⟩=⟨4cosh⁡ϕcos⁡θ,4cosh⁡ϕsin⁡θ,4sinh⁡ϕ⟩

where θ∈[0,2π) and ϕ∈R.

Therefore, the second component of f is 4cosh⁡ϕsin⁡θ.
